summary: This is an opening excerpt from the fiction piece 'A Vessel for Offering' by Darren R. Hawkins, labeled Book 15 part 1. An unnamed man crawls through cramped ducts and vents, pausing to catch his breath while his flashlight strap keeps loosening and the air smells foul. Much of the passage is his wry complaint about the right-angle turns, which he hates more than anything, and his sense that the plan to get here was a bad idea.
one_line: An unnamed man crawls through foul, cramped ventilation ducts, cursing the right-angle turns and the bad plan that brought him there.
key_facts: The excerpt is titled 'A Vessel for Offering' by Darren R. Hawkins and is labeled 'Book 15 — part 1'.
The protagonist moves through ducts and vents by pushing forward with his elbows, planting them on a seam for traction, and dragging his body behind.
He has covered a few hundred meters of constant inchworm contractions through a space barely large enough for his shoulders to pass.
His flashlight strap has been pulling loose for the last ten minutes, and the beam jiggles too much for him to judge his progress.
The air smells of a noxious chemical combination of sweat, dust, mildew and other assorted skanks rather than the clean, coppery stink of sheet metal and coolant.
He considers giving up and passing out, letting some other idiot worry about getting him out.
He says the planner of the scheme should be given a citation, 'With a hammer. To the forehead. Until he was freaking dead.'
He says it is not the dirt, heat or odor that bothers him but the intersections, meaning the right angles, which he hates absolutely.
He lists the joints capable of a ninety degree maneuver as the pelvis, knee, elbow, sometimes the neck, and a few other odds and ends.
He compares himself to raw bratwurst crammed into sausage casings as he forces his way through a skintight metallic tube.
He has been twisting his body through these tight spaces for the last hour or better.
He describes a claustrophobic part of his mind as a hysterically gibbering claustrophobe chained up in a closet in the back of his mind.
